speculative_claims: In demography, 'net internal migration' measures the difference between the number of people moving into a region from other parts of the same country and those leaving that region for other domestic destinations, normalized per 1,000 residents.
This metric excludes international immigration and natural population changes (births and deaths), focusing purely on domestic population redistribution.
A positive value indicates a net influx of domestic residents, whereas a negative value indicates a net population loss to other regions.
These migration patterns reflect Italy's long-standing socio-economic divide between the wealthier, highly industrialized North and the economically disadvantaged South (Mezzogiorno).
Northern regions like Emilia-Romagna and Lombardy attract domestic migrants due to stronger job markets, better public infrastructure, and prominent universities.

Conversely, net population losses in southern regions like Calabria and Molise exacerbate the challenges of 'brain drain' and demographic aging, making it increasingly difficult for these areas to sustain local economies and public services.

The 2019 dataset serves as an important baseline representing demographic trends immediately prior to the COVID-19 pandemic, which subsequently disrupted traditional migration patterns and accelerated remote work trends across Italy.
